concepts.gloss_en: word/thing/matter (a spoken word or an object)

reason_for_human: The written form דבר covers two distinct words here, and the proofs vocalize them differently. דָּבָר (occ 1407, 1842) means 'word/thing' — explicitly 'הַנִּקְרָא דָּבָר' and 'כָּל דָּבָר', while דַּבָּר (occ 1726, 1899) is glossed by the text itself as 'לְשׁוֹן מַנְהִיג וּמוֹשֵׁל' (leader/ruler), from 'דַּבָּר אֶחָד לְדוֹר'. Different vocalization + different meaning = split; the two דָּבָר usages share one lexical word so they stay merged.
